title: Quaquanantuck / Quantuck Bay and Creek
summary: A western Southampton creek, bay, meadow, and purchase-record name preserved in seventeenth-century sources.
introduction_content: Quaquanantuck is a western Southampton locality connected with Quogue, Quantuck Bay, and surrounding meadows. Shortened and variant forms include Quaganantuck, Quaguanantuck, Quaquantuck, Quagwanantuck, Quaqua, Quago, Quogo, Quaquananuck, Quaquanantuck, and Quantuck.
history_content: The name appears in town records, meadow privileges, boundary descriptions, and the contested Quogue purchase landscape. Dated references appear in the Historic Timeline so each claim carries its own citation.
translation_content:
Quaquanantuck is interpreted as a cove or estuary where the land or water quakes or trembles, referring to the shaking marshes around the waters now known as Quantuck Bay. Quantuck may be an abbreviated form, or separately understood as a long tidal stream or creek.

Why Place Names Matter

“Each language is deeply rooted to the land and offers an ideal opportunity to connect a name to a place.”

— Geographic Names Victoria, What we do: Aboriginal place naming (2025), Our rich Aboriginal history
preservation_content: Quaquanantuck connects the Quogue purchase, Quantuck Bay, creek, meadow, neck, and path names in western Southampton, preserving how Indigenous place-names continued to structure colonial land records and local geography.
